lc_person: Antonio Rafael de la Cova, born 1950; historian, West Virginia University Ph.D. (1994), author of Cuban Confederate Colonel: The Life of Ambrosio José Gonzales (2003).
item_person: Rafael de la Cova, nineteenth-century sculptor; Wikidata records birth in the 1850s and death in 1896, alongside a conflicting 1950 birth imported from LC.

evidence.says: LC identifies De la Cova, Antonio Rafael, 1950-. Its source note for Cuban Confederate colonel (2003) gives birth year 1950 from the publisher data sheet. Other source notes identify a history teacher with a West Virginia University Ph.D. LC also links to Q55347354.

The item is labeled Rafael de la Cova and describes a nineteenth-century sculptor. It lists sculpture as occupation, the Guaicaipuro monument as a notable work, birth in the 1850s and death in 1896. It also carries LC identifier n2003037862 and a second birth statement, year 1950, explicitly sourced to that LC authority.

West Virginia University lists Antonio Rafael de la Cova as author of the 1994 dissertation Ambrosio Jose Gonzales: A Cuban Confederate colonel. Author, institution, year and biographical subject match the graph’s AHA dissertation evidence, despite the different recorded title.

The publisher identifies Antonio Rafael de la Cova as teaching history at the University of South Carolina Columbia, holding a history Ph.D. from West Virginia University, and authoring Cuban Confederate Colonel and The Moncada Attack.

notes: The evidence indicates conflation of the sculptor with the historian’s authority data, rather than a name variant or simple birth-year typo. LC fits the graph’s dissertation author. Its reciprocal Wikidata link does not resolve the contradiction. No separate QID for the historian was verified; 1950 applies to the LC historian.
